title: The principal open in the strict localization at infinity
statement: Let K:Type u be an algebraically closed field and n a natural number. Put B=Spec K[x_0,...,x_n], b:B->Spec K, Y=P^1_B [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], g:Y->B, and i:B->Y the infinity section. Let e:Spec K[x_0,...,x_(n+1)] ~= A^1_B be any scheme isomorphism, and j=e followed by the ordinary affine chart. For an algebraically closed field Omega:Type u and s:Spec Omega->B, put t=s followed by i and y=t(closedPoint Omega). Use the strict localization R=O^sh_(Y,t), rho:Spec R->Y from [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], and the canonical K-algebra structure on kappa(y) induced by g followed by b. There exist a natural number a<n+2 and h in R such that both trdeg_K kappa(s) and trdeg_K kappa(y) [def-kun-transcendence-degree] equal a, h is a nonzero element of the maximal ideal of R, and the pullback of j along rho is isomorphic to Spec R[1/h].

proof.text: For a point of polynomial (n+1)-space, [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] identifies its residue transcendence degree with the finite dimension a of its closure. This is at most n+1, the dimension of the polynomial spectrum. The infinity section is a closed immersion, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso] identifies its residue field with that of the base point; composition naturality shows the isomorphism respects K.

The infinity chart is Spec A[z], where A is the polynomial base ring. The strict localization has closed point over infinity by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure]. Every point of a local spectrum specializes to its closed point, so rho factors through this chart. Pull z back along the induced explicit ring map alpha:A[z]->R to define h.

The chart map is ind-etale by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-affine-chart-ind-etale]. Its filtered etale presentation is a filtered colimit of flat algebras, so it is flat. The variable z is regular in A[z], hence h is regular in the nonzero ring R and h is not zero. The two projective-line charts meet in D(z), so rho inverse-image of the ordinary chart is D(h). Infinity lies outside that chart, so the closed point lies outside D(h), giving h in the maximal ideal.

The pullback open immersion and Spec R[1/h]->Spec R have the same range D(h). Mathlib IsOpenImmersion.isoOfRangeEq identifies their sources. Transport along e by the pullback universal property. All constructions work at nonclosed base points and at n=0.

theorem affineLine_infinity_strictLocal_model
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] (n : ℕ)
    (e : Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 2)) K)) ≅
      AffineSpace PUnit.{u + 1} (Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) K))))
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) K))) :
    let B := Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) K))
    let b := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) K)))
    let Y := AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveLine B
    let g := Y ↘ B
    let j := e.hom ≫ ProjectiveLine.affineChart B
    let t := s ≫ ProjectiveLine.infinity B
    let y := t (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω)
    letI : Algebra K (Y.residueField y) := ((g ≫ b).residueFieldAlgebraMap y).toAlgebra
    ∃ a : ℕ, a < n + 2 ∧
      residueFieldTrdeg b (s (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω)) = (a : Cardinal.{u}) ∧
      Algebra.trdeg K (Y.residueField y) = (a : Cardinal.{u}) ∧
      ∃ h : strictHenselizationRing t, h ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal _ ∧ h ≠ 0 ∧
        Nonempty (pullback j (strictHenselizationStructuralMap t) ≅
          Spec (.of (Localization.Away h)))
